title: Effective etale equivalence-relation quotients in algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A,R$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and let $s,t:R\to A$ be morphisms. Assume $(s,t):R\to A\times_S A$ is a monomorphism of sheaves and identifies $R(H)$ with an equivalence relation on $A(H)$ for every $S$-scheme $H$. Assume $s,t$ are chartwise etale [def-sfb-space-chartwise-etale-morphism]; they need not be representable by schemes. Let $F$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site] of $H\mapsto A(H)/R(H)$, and let $p:A\to F$ be the quotient map. Then $F$ is an algebraic space over $S$, $p$ is chartwise etale, and every map $h_H\to F$ from an $S$-scheme lifts to $A$ on an etale covering of $H$. The canonical map $R\to A\times_F A$ is an isomorphism, with projections $s,t$. Here all fibre products of spaces are those of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For every fppf sheaf $G$, composition with $p$ is a bijection between maps $F\to G$ and maps $u:A\to G$ satisfying $us=ut$. No quasi-compactness, separatedness, Noetherian or finite type assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Put $P(H)=A(H)/R(H)$. First identify the kernel relation of $p$, without assuming $F$ algebraic. If $a,b\in A(H)$ have $p(a)=p(b)$, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] gives an fppf covering on which $[a]=[b]$ in $P$. Equality of equivalence classes supplies sections $r_i$ of $R$ with endpoints $a,b$. On overlaps the $r_i$ agree because $(s,t)$ is monic. Since $R$ is a sheaf, they glue uniquely to $r\in R(H)$. Conversely such an $r$ makes $[a]=[b]$, hence $p(a)=p(b)$. Thus $R(H)\to A(H)\times_{F(H)}A(H)$ is bijective for every $H$. The inverse commutes with restrictions by uniqueness, giving $R\simeq A\times_F A$ with the specified projections. This fibre product is initially taken among sheaves.

source.place: Tag 046O (lemma-quotient-pre-equivalence), local-equality criterion; monomorphy and the sheaf axiom give effectivity

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $a:h_V\to A$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Set $B=R\times_{t,A,a}h_V$ and $D=h_V\times_{a,A,s\operatorname{pr}_R}B$. These are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Their sections are triples $(v,r,w)$ with $a(v)=s(r)$ and $t(r)=a(w)$. The map $D\to B$ is the base change of $a$, hence representable etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. The map $B\to h_V$ is the base change of $t$ and is chartwise etale. Composition and base change in [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] show that $D\to h_V$, $(v,r,w)\mapsto w$, is chartwise etale; interchange $s,t$ for the other projection. Moreover $j_D:D\to h_{V\times_S V}$ is monic, and $D(H)$ identifies with the equivalence relation $p(a(v))=p(a(w))$ by step 1. Thus, as sheaves, $D=h_V\times_Fh_V$.

proof.text: The space $D$ is a scheme. For any representable etale chart $h_W\to D$, the composite $W\to V$ is etale by step 2. It is locally finitely presented by [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence locally of finite type: the finite presentation in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] is in particular a finite algebra generating set, as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply clause (a) of [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target] to $W\to V\times_S V\to V$. Hence $W\to V\times_S V$ is locally of finite type for every chart, exactly the hypothesis of [lem-sfb-space-lft-monomorphism-separated-lqf] for the monomorphism $j_D$. That result gives separatedness and chartwise local quasi-finiteness of $j_D$. Its target $V\times_S V$ is a scheme, so [lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable] represents $D$ by a scheme. Its projections to $V$ are etale scheme maps: the identity chart of this represented scheme and step 2 give representable etaleness, which agrees with scheme etaleness by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests].

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] to the scheme equivalence relation $D\rightrightarrows V$. Write $Q=(h_V/D)^{\#}$ and $q:h_V\to Q$. Then $Q$ is algebraic, $q$ is representable surjective etale, and $D=h_V\times_Qh_V$. The universal property gives $c:Q\to F$ with $cq=pa$. We check local bijectivity. If $x,y\in Q(H)$ have equal $c$-images, take etale local lifts $v,w$ to $V$, using the lifting clause of that same node and a common refinement. Their equal $pa$-images give a section of $D$ by step 2, so $q(v)=q(w)$; thus $x,y$ agree locally. For $f\in F(H)$, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] gives fppf local representatives in $P$, hence, after choosing representatives of those classes, sections $b_i\in A(H_i)$. By [lem-a1-representable-etale-fppf-local-lifting], each $b_i$ lifts to $V$ on an etale covering which is also fppf. The sections $q(v_i)$ then lift $f$ on the resulting composite fppf covering. Thus $c$ is locally injective and locally surjective, and [lem-galois-set-sheaf-local-bijection-isomorphism] makes it an isomorphism. In particular $F$ is algebraic.

source.place: Tag 046P (lemma-quotient-pre-equivalence-relation-restrict), explicit local-injectivity and local-surjectivity argument; spaces.tex Tag 02WW (theorem-presentation)

proof.text: Under $c:Q\simeq F$, the composite $pa=cq:h_V\to F$ is representable surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Apply [lem-trf-space-etale-source-atlas-detection], clause (3), to the atlas $a:h_V\to A$ and $p:A\to F$. It gives chartwise etaleness of $p$, without claiming representability of $p$. For a map $h_H\to F$, the local-lifting clause of [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient], transported through $c$, gives an etale covering on which it lifts to $V$, hence to $A$ via $a$. Step 1 now identifies $R$ with the algebraic-space fibre product $A\times_F A$: its sectionwise identification is precisely the sheaf fibre product used by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 03FS (lemma-etale-local), (2) implies (1); spaces.tex Tag 02WW; spaces-groupoids.tex Tag 046O

proof.text: For an fppf sheaf $G$, any equalizing map $u:A\to G$ descends sectionwise to $P\to G$ by $[a]\mapsto u(a)$. It is well defined because equivalent sections are the endpoints of an $R$-section and $us=ut$; it is natural because $u$ is. Conversely a map $P\to G$ gives such a $u$, and these operations are inverse since every equivalence class has a representative. The defining universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] then extends $P\to G$ uniquely to $F\to G$, giving exactly the required bijection by composition with $p$. All constructions used the stated universes and arbitrary etale atlases; no quasi-compactness, separation, Noetherian or finite type hypothesis on the original spaces was used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q28-8db0faf16 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery against its sources and the 16 cited statements; review.md has the step-by-step checks. Shape: the item becomes a 6-step split with no new nodes; it is not a re-split. The statement is unchanged and true: it is the étale case of Stacks Tag 04S6 condition (1) (bootstrap.tex, theorem-final-bootstrap). The proof follows that reduction: restrict to an étale scheme atlas (Tag 046P); j is monic and locally of finite type, so it is locally quasi-finite and separated, so the restricted relation D is a scheme. Step 1 writes out the omitted local-equality details of Tag 046O and glues by monomorphy. Step 3 hypotheses checked: W→V étale gives W→V×V locally of finite type by clause (a) of lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target; this is exactly the input of lem-sfb-space-lft-monomorphism-separated-lqf, whose output is exactly the input of lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable, which needs no quasi-compactness. Step 4 checks local injectivity and surjectivity of c:Q→F, using lem-a1-representable-etale-fppf-local-lifting (no algebraicity of F needed) and the local-bijection lemma for sheaves of sets. The equalizing condition pa∘s_D=pa∘t_D needed for c is left implicit; it is one line from ps=pt. Step 5 uses clause (3) of the source-atlas-detection lemma once F is algebraic. Step 6 is genuinely elementary. Edge cases checked: empty spaces, diagonal R, a swap relation on a disjoint union; no quasi-compactness or separatedness is used. No duplicate: the trf/sfb scheme-relation, bootstrap and groupoid-stack nodes all differ. Batch 5: each of the 7 flagged citations is a generic algebraic-space foundation (closure properties of étale maps, the scheme étale-relation quotient, local lifting, representability criteria). None is the trace formula, Poincaré duality, or a step of their proofs, so all are kept. I accept the 10 tool_uses as generic tools. No fixes.
